target.projectDescription: TensorFlow is a large numerical-computation library: a C++ runtime (grappler, distributed_runtime, kernels, TFLite flatbuffers) with an extensive Python API layer (tensorflow/python, tensorflow/keras, tensorflow/lite/python), Python build/CI tooling (tensorflow/tools, tensorflow/compiler), a Python gRPC debug server (tfdbg, tensorflow/python/debug), and argparse/absl CLI entry points. The Python database covers only the Python files of the tree; the C++ servers (worker/grpc servers, tf.data service) are out of scope for this pass.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attacker-relevant input boundaries in the Python layer: (1) the tfdbg gRPC debug server: an unauthenticated grpc.server listener whose SendEvents/SendTracebacks/SendSourceFiles methods receive Event protos from any client that can reach the port; the message bodies are JSON-decoded (plugin metadata, core metadata) and reassembled GraphDefs are ParseFromString-decoded, then handed to on_value_event/on_graph_def/on_core_metadata_event callbacks and, in grpc_debug_test_server, the grpc_path field flows into an os.path.join; (2) CLI entry points: argparse/absl parsers (339 non-test add_argument sites), sys.argv reads (tfdbg CLIs, tflite_convert, pip_package setup, multi_process_lib), raw input() prompts; (3) environment variables: ~74-82 non-test os.environ/os.getenv sites, notably TF_CONFIG JSON cluster specs and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; (4) files/models: 148 non-test open() calls (SavedModel/TFLite/keras configs, keras config json.load, tfdbg CLI config), gfile.Open reads, proto ParseFromString (72 non-test sites); (5) outbound HTTP fetches whose responses are trusted: tf.tpu client and keras data_utils urlopen. Command-execution sinks concentrate in tensorflow/lite/python/convert.py (Popen with shell=True, the deprecated toco binary path), tensorflow/lite/schema/upgrade_schema.py (flatc), slurm_cluster_resolver (nvidia-smi), and tensorflow/tools build/CI/packaging scripts; several more os.system sites live in tflite testing harnesses. Normal build-tool command execution is not automatically a vulnerability.

inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Most command-execution sites in this snapshot are build, CI, doc, packaging or GPU-discovery tooling with static or internally-derived operands. The runtime TFLite path (convert.py _run_toco_binary) passes a joined string to Popen with shell=True, and the tfdbg gRPC server accepts unauthenticated network input; these are recorded as candidates for the LLM labeling step, not as vulnerabilities. Normal command execution functionality is not automatically treated as a vulnerability.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile followed by codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) and codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware for 'import subprocess as _subprocess' / 'import json as _json', only genuine resolved calls into external modules
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name, function/method name); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise. The six.moves.urllib indirection (tpu client: 'from six.moves.urllib import request' then request.urlopen) is invisible to API graphs, so the network-fetch boundary is matched at AST level

exclusions: test files and test harnesses: any path under a tests/, test/ or testing/ directory, conftest.py, and *_test.py / *_test_base.py basenames (bazel convention; this also removes tensorflow/tools/test/, tensorflow/lite/testing/, tensorflow/lite/experimental/mlir/testing/, multi_worker_test_base.py and the *_test.py files that contain most os.system sites)
tensorflow-safe-db (pristine copy in the source tree) is not part of the database, so no duplicate rows are expected
logging-only helpers (print / logger.<level> parents) are excluded from the cmd_format sink family
the 7 third_party files inside the database are kept (negligible volume)

uncoveredCases: tensorflow/python/debug/lib/grpc_debug_server.py:148-178 - per-field attribute reads of the network event (event.summary.value[0], event.graph_def, event.log_message.message) are not extracted as individual rows; the SendEvents parameter row and the json.loads/ParseFromString rows mark the boundary instead

tensorflow/python/debug/lib/grpc_debug_test_server.py:93-98 - 'core_metadata["grpc_path"]' dict read flows into os.path.join; dict-key reads are not extracted as a separate family (the on_core_metadata_event parameter and json.loads rows cover the entry)

six.moves indirection: tpu/client/client.py imports request from six.moves.urllib and keras data_utils uses urlopen imported conditionally per Python version; API graphs cannot resolve these, so urlopen/urlretrieve matching relies on the ast match_kind (bare 'urlopen' name or 'request'/'urllib' receiver prefix)

import aliases: 'import subprocess as _subprocess' (lite/python/convert.py), 'import json as _json' (lite/python/op_hint.py), 'import os as _os' (platform/tf_logging, resource_loader, convert.py) - API graphs are expected to resolve _subprocess.Popen/_json.loads through the import table (match_kind api); the AST fallback additionally accepts these alias prefixes (match_kind ast)

no 'from subprocess import ...' / 'from os import <exec>' form exists in the tree, so bare-name execution sinks are only matched for the distinctive names system/popen/getoutput/getstatusoutput; bare run/call/Popen/check_call/check_output are too collision-prone and are excluded (this gap is not exercised in this snapshot)
